# Where the client departs from the original

A catalog of every place found where this client does not do what the original Anarchy Online client does, so that
each can be decided: **port** the original's behaviour, or **leave** the client's. Made 2026-11-18.

## How to use it

Every entry has a number (`MOV-004`). Answer with numbers: "port MOV-004, CMB-011; leave the rest of Combat", or mark
the boxes in this file. An entry says what the original does (as the code's comments or the notes state it), what the
client does today, what a player notices, and where it is in the code.

- **Kind** says what sort of departure it is:
  - `OWN-RULE`: the client knowingly does otherwise.
  - `SIMPLIFIED`: an approximation or a stand-in.
  - `GUESS`: the original was not read: inferred or measured.
  - `SAFETY`: a guard or fallback the original lacks.
  - `MISSING`: the original does it, the client does not.
  - `ADDITION`: the client has it, the original does not.
- **Weight** is how much a player notices it: `high` (often, or it changes what one can do), `medium` (now and
  then, or plain but cosmetic), `low` (rare, subtle or internal). It is a judgement, made to sort the list.
- **(notes only)** marks an entry that rests on the project's notes and could not be found in the code either way.

## How it was made, and what it is not

- Seventeen readers went through the whole client (120,000 lines of code in `crates/`) and the project's notes in
  `docs/`, and wrote down every stated departure: 1767 raw entries. Every one quoted its source line, and each quote
  was checked by program against the file.
- A second pass, by area, folded the repeats, checked every notes-only entry against today's code and dropped the
  ones the code had since put right, and dropped what was only "not tried live". 936 entries were left.
- It lists what the code and the notes **say**. A place where the client departs from the original without anybody
  having written so (a rule fitted long ago and never marked, an original behaviour nobody has read) is not in it.
  What the original does is given as the comments give it; it was not read again from the decompiled code for this
  catalog.
- "The original" under ADDITION entries means the original has no such thing; whether a thing is wanted is yours
  to say.

## Movement

### Movement: the client knowingly does otherwise (3)

#### `MOV-001` Own flight also read from worn items and running programs

- OWN-RULE, medium
- Original: switches to fly mode (7) when the server's spell list runs spell 0xcf92 (FUN_100a8107) and back when that list ends
- Client: also treats a running program or a worn item with the fly spell as flying, since no capture shows a list for a worn item and it was not seen whether the server sends one at login or zoning; not tried live
- A player notices: a worn jetpack or Yalmaha may start flight where the original would wait for the server's list
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:341`; `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:8688`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:3576`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): Of the client's three sources of own flight, the worn item's is the original's own: the original runs an item's wear spell list on the client when it is put on (the same path the client ports for 0xcf76, `item::worn_sets`), so a worn item's 0xcf92 enters fly mode there too (FUN_100a8107). The running-program source stands in for the server's spell list after a login or a zoning with a flight program running: no capture shows whether the server sends that list again then, and removing it could leave a flier on foot in the air. It needs a capture of a zoning (or login) while a flight program runs; until then it stays.

#### `MOV-002` Sliding along a room's edge when a step leaves the rooms

- OWN-RULE, low
- Original: not stated (n3RoomSurface_t::VetoPosition refuses the place)
- Client: if still out of the rooms after stepping back, tries moving along either axis, else not at all
- A player notices: a character slides along an interior wall instead of stopping dead
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/vehicle.rs:341`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): Read: the original's refusal of a place outside the rooms is n3RoomSurface_t::VetoPosition (0x10015587) inside the sweep against the room surfaces, which the client does not have (MOV-026); the client tests the room cells after the step-back loop instead. Dropping the axis slide without the room surfaces would let a step end outside every room (the step-back loop stops a tenth short), so it stays until n3RoomSurface_t is ported.

- Client: a worn Yalmaha sets Scale 20 and adds 300 RunSpeed as temporary stats; the client saves the old scale and gives it back when taken off, also when the server's list said 20 in between; with none saved (logging in on the craft) the character stays small after leaving it until the server says otherwise
- A player notices: size and flying speed come back by client bookkeeping; wrong size possible after login on a Yalmaha
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:12340`; `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:1451`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:3990`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave

#### `MOV-004` Own walking and collision where a playfield has no surfaces (and with noclip)

- Original: Vehicle_t::Run and EnsureSurfaceAlignment against n3TilemapSurface_t, in every playfield; collision from surfaces
- Client: in a generated dungeon, room playfields without surfaces (missions) and with noclip, the client's own steps are used: the props' visible meshes or triangles, wall sliding along the walls (a single axis tried after), fixed jump speed 7 and gravity 10, floor probing; MAO_VISUAL_COLLISION forces them
- A player notices: walking, jumping and collision feel and behave differently in such playfields
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:8771`; `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:6661-6662`; `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:8845-8870`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:2872`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:2875`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:2923`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The client's own step code runs only where the playfield has no 0xf424d surfaces (generated mission dungeons, rooms) or with noclip. The original never lacks a surface there: indoors its vehicle walks n3RoomSurface_t (per-room surfaces placed with the room's transform, see MOV-026), which the client has not ported; it uses the room floors' triangles instead. Porting n3RoomSurface_t (closest point, room transforms, VetoRoomTransition) is a large N3.dll port, well over the 40-minute bound, and wants a live check in a mission. Noclip is the client's own key (MOV-032).

#### `MOV-009` Others count as moving for a fixed 700 ms

- SIMPLIFIED, low
- Original: not stated
- Client: a character is shown moving if its place changed in the last 700 ms (creatures 900 ms)
- A player notices: walk animation may linger or stop early
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:5372`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19): The original moves another character between the server's messages by its movement status (`CharMovementStatus_t`, vtable 0x101616f4: the transition table FUN_1006cb58 sets the forward/strafe/turn/jump states, 1/2 forward, 3/4 reverse, 5..8 strafes, 0x15 full stop) and its vehicle's speed for the mode (FUN_1006f9eb); its walk animation follows that status (FUN_1006c370). The client does not move others between reports at all (net.rs `apply`: `e.0 = p`, no dead reckoning; only path-walked creatures move, `walk_paths`), so taking "moving" from the start/stop types instead of the 700/900 ms since the place changed would play a walk on a body that stands still until the next report. The faithful port is the others' dead reckoning by that status (speed by mode, the stops, the server paths' creatures), which changes how every other character moves and can only be judged on screen; the captures hold no server-sent 0x54111123 lines to check the rate against (0 in the arete/door/events captures). Left for a port of the others' movement together with MOV-015.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The original keeps another character moving by its movement state machine (the start/stop types of FUN_1006cb58: 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, 7/8, 0x15 full stop), not by a time since its place changed; porting means a per-character state from those types for everyone, plus the server paths' creatures (which move without such messages, the 900 ms case). That is a change to the whole others' animation path, more than this low entry is worth tonight; noted for a later port together with MOV-015.

#### `MOV-014` Seated character cannot move or jump

- GUESS, low
- Original: what a jump does while seated was not read (only the sit toggle's LeaveSit ends sit mode; turns are taken in any mode)
- Client: forward, back, sidesteps and jump do nothing while seated; the sit key is the only way up (taken from the user's word)
- A player notices: a seated character cannot walk or jump
- Where: `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:1530`; `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:8650`; `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:4355`; `docs/ORIGINAL_AUDIT.md:27`
- Decision: [x] port  [ ] leave
- Done (2026-11-19): The guess is now the original's rule, read: every movement first passes `N3Msg_MovementChanged` (Gamecode 0x10018bc4), which asks the character's `CharMovementStatus_t` (vtable 0x101616f4) slot 3, FUN_1006c6f4, whether the type is allowed in the current mode. In the sit mode (8) it refuses forward/back and the sidesteps (1..8), the jump (0xf), the walk/run switches (0x18/0x19) and the full report, and takes the turns (9..0xe), swimming (0x1a) and the getting up (0x25): nothing is sent, nothing moves. So the client's "seated cannot move or jump, only the sit key stands up" was right. Added the one missing piece: GUI.dll `SlotMovementForward` 0x100289f5 (and Back 0x10028a46, StrafeLeft 0x10028b05, StrafeRight 0x10028b58) send AFCM 0xe3 when the mode is 8, `FlowControlModule_t::MovementWhileSittingMessage` 0x1002888f, which raises the tip event `OnMovementWhileSitting`; the client now raises it on each press/release of those keys while sitting (not sleeping/lounging, modes 0xb/0xc). The game's tip files have no tip for that event, so nothing shows. Tests: net::movement_tests::sitting_is_held_until_getting_up (unchanged, passes). Not looked at: the walk toggle while seated goes another road (`SlotMovementWalkToggle` → `N3Msg_PerformSpecialAction`), left as it is.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): What forward, back and jump do while seated in the original is decided in the transition table FUN_1006cb58's per-mode handling and was not read to the end tonight; the client's rule is the user's own word ("seated cannot move"), so it is kept until the table is read.

#### `MOV-017` Client goes back to a place the server reports

- SAFETY, medium

- Client: a full report more than 5 m from us that is none of the places we told it in the last 4 s makes the client go back there (`own_report`)

The original ignores all of the server's movement messages of its own character: FUN_1006c20f (CharDCMoveIIR_t's dynel lookup) clears a message that is not ToBePassedOn (one from the server) when its dynel is the client control dynel and returns none, so the activation FUN_1006bd94 does nothing; only a locally made message (to be passed on) is stamped with the current place and UpdateLastMotionMessageData. The captures agree that the server echoes every own movement (same counts both ways; 36 of ~8,700 echoes name a place up to ~3.5 m off). Real put-backs still come through SetPos and N3Teleport, which the client follows. The far report is still written to the log ("the server names us at ... and stay"). No unit test (game-loop code); built.

#### `TGT-013` Target sent as "none" on entering and when lost

- SAFETY, low
- Original: sends its selection when it changes; what it does on entering was not read
- Client: sends LookAt with no target once on entering and whenever a target is lost, so a taken-over character's old target does not catch targetless casts
- A player notices: no stale target after a session takeover
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/net.rs:8639`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:551`; `docs/LIVE_TEST_LIST.md:103`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19): Read now. The original sends `LookAt` (0x2252445f, `LookAtIIR_t` built by FUN_100754b2) only from `N3Msg_SelectedTarget` (0x10017790 → FUN_1003fd9f → FUN_1003babc → FUN_1003b2ee / FUN_1003b951), when the selection changes (or always for a character's identity, type 50000). Losing the target is the original's too: `TargetingModule_t::RemoveTargetIDMessage` (GUI 0x100267d4, AFCM 0x113 with the gone identity, when it is the current target) → `RemoveTarget` 0x100264e3 → `SetTarget(none)` 0x10026308 → AFCM 0x13/0x126 → `N3Msg_SelectedTarget(none)`, which sends the empty `LookAt` since the selection changed; so the client's send on loss is faithful. On entering the original sends nothing (the module's `InitialiseMessage` 0x10026e12 sets no target; nothing else calls `N3Msg_SelectedTarget`), so the client's one empty `LookAt` on entering is its own. Not removed: it was added for a problem seen live (2026-11-10: a character taken over after a quick relog kept its server-side target, and a self-buff landed on it), which the original would have as well; removing it changes the messages sent and re-opens that. Recommend KEEP the entering send (the user's call); the loss send needs nothing.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): Kept: removing the LookAt "none" on entering would change what is sent, and the original's behaviour on entering was not read; the client sends it because a character taken over (a quick relog) keeps its server-side target, which then catches targetless casts.

Read tonight: the creature's constructor (FUN_1005d0b1, and FUN_1009cda2) calls FUN_1003cf4f(0x78), which sets the standing action (+0x10) and, only when the creature's set has one, the standing animation handle (+0x34). FUN_1003cce2, the stance logic, reads +0x34 and nothing else starts an animation then. So such a creature's CAT body is never given an animation by Gamecode. What it is then drawn as depends on DisplaySystem's VisualCATMesh with an empty animation stack, and that was not settled. Either it hands CATRender_t a null animation, so that FUN_10054d16 poses nothing and SetMesh (randy31 catrender set_mesh) has filled the buffers' texture coordinates only, or it hands it a blend that poses every bone at identity, as the client's empty AnimStack::pose would. ### Nano programs: an approximation or a stand-in (24)

#### `NAN-004` NCU memory in use is summed by the client

- SIMPLIFIED, medium
- Original: The NCU in use is stat 180 (title "NCU (%u/%u)" from stats 180 and 181, FUN_100d7689); the note says the original works it out as the sum of the running nanos' quality stat.
- Client: The server does not send stat 180 for one's own character, so the running nanos' costs are summed for the strip and the NCU window; a missing stat 181 reads 0.
- A player notices: The NCU figure may differ from the server's when a nano is missing from the list.
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/ui.rs:1088`; `crates/mao-client/src/ncu.rs:244`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:1695`
- Decision: [x] port  [ ] leave
- Done (2026-11-19): The taking-away the earlier note could not find is Gamecode FUN_10051041 at 0x1005131b..0x1005138e: after FUN_1004f34f took the nano off the running list, stat 180 = stat 180 - the nano's stat 54, under exactly the add's rule (flags 0x10000 set, none of 0x4000/0x8000/0x100); its three callers (FUN_100517f3 0x1005188e, FUN_10051b6f 0x10051bde, FUN_100726e5 0x1007270c) all push 1 for the flag that asks for it. So the original's running total is the sum over the running list of the counting nanos, which the client computes (ncu::ncu_cost). The one departure left in ncu_cost, the client's own "a cost of 999 is free" rule, is dropped: the original adds stat 54 whatever it is (over the game's 10964 nanos, 2930 carry 999 but only four have the counting flags: three "Destruction" programs and one unlisted one). #### `NAN-038` Cast effect: hand cords draw nothing; phases 3-4 (projectile, impact) not played

- MISSING, medium (notes only)
- Original: _GfxControlSpell1_t phases 3-4: projectile _GfxControlNano0_t from the hands to the target, impact _GfxControlNano1_t over the bones; hand cords (kind 1003) lay links.
- Client: Only hand flares and the line between hands; cords draw nothing; timeline fixed (phase 1 0-6 s, beam 4-5 s), so in practice a cast shows the hand flares only.
- A player notices: No projectile or impact from casts.
- Where: `docs/ORIGINAL_AUDIT.md:267`
- Decision: [x] port  [ ] leave
- Done (2026-11-19): Nothing to port: the client already shows what the original shows. The hand cords draw nothing in the original either: Spell1's phase 1 (FUN_100f29ea) makes its words 29–30 cords with the point `CreateGfxControl(id, Vector3)` (Gamecode FUN_100cea4b → `_GfxControlCord_t` FUN_100d6420), whose locator takes the cord's flag bit 2 as its "lays links" byte (FUN_101067af's last argument); every cord a cast template names has flags 5 (bit 2 clear), so the cord's set-position (FUN_100d69d8, called each frame by FUN_100f2bab with the hand's place) only moves its locator (FUN_101064f7) and never lays a link (FUN_100d6323), and its run (FUN_100d5f5a) only ages links it has none of. Phases 3–4 (FUN_100f3f30 calls FUN_100f3e99 projectile / FUN_100f31b1 impact only when word 33, +0x11c, is 0; NextState FUN_100f2617 retimes only then too) are on in exactly two templates, 9000 and 9002, which are one word short and read word 33 as 0 (FUN_10106dc8); no other template refers to them, and no nano program or item names them (or anything containing them) in its cast, hit, running, tracer, gather or impact effect. Only one kind-1008 `_GfxControlNano1_t` template exists (8011) and only Spell1s name it. So in the original no cast ever throws a projectile or plays an impact, and no cord draws. The Original line of the entry ("hand cords lay links") is not what the code does. Proof as a game-data test: mao-formats `a_cast_effect_lays_no_cords_and_throws_nothing` (MAO_GAME), which also confirms the 180 cast templates.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The missing parts are whole effect classes of DisplaySystem.dll: _GfxControlSpell1_t's phases 3-4 (a _GfxControlNano0_t projectile from the hands to the target and a _GfxControlNano1_t impact over the bones) and the hand cords (kind 1003 links). Each is its own renderer port with its own gfxtweak data; well beyond the 40-minute bound, and only checkable by pictures of a live cast.

The question is the original's InviteDialog_c (FUN_100ae840/FUN_100af0ed): the text ChatFriendList_InvitedToPrivateGroupDialogText with the inviter's name, a multi-select list of the chat windows by name (FUN_100aef3a, starting with those that already show the group chosen), and Yes/No. Yes puts the group into the chosen windows and takes it out of the others, auto-subscribing windows included (FUN_100a74cb → FUN_1009d5cc / FUN_1009d87a), then joins. No or closing declines. The inviter becomes a "Recent Messages" row on the chat server (FUN_100a6b54 → FUN_100a6487; net.rs recent_message). Invitations are now taken and their question shown even while the chat window is shut. Departures, both guesses or client limits: the original puts its "default window" first in the list, and the client has no default-window flag (CHT-059); pressing a marked row while the question is already up opens a second dialog in the original but not here. That Yes is answer index 0 is read from FUN_100a74cb's branch, not seen live. Tests: chatwindow::tests::{an_invitation_waits_is_declined_or_is_dropped, an_invitation_is_marked_then_asked_with_its_chat_windows}, friends::tests::a_press_on_a_row_opens_or_shuts_the_tell_window. Whole mao-client bin: 726 passed.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): Not ported for budget: the original's invitation question (FUN_100a76c9) carries a list of the chat windows to put the private group in, and ChatPGInviteAction 2 only marks the invitation in the friends list; the client's box has no list and the group goes to the windows that take new channels. Porting needs a window chooser inside the question box and the friends list's invitation mark (which itself needs CHT-050's rows), not done tonight.

- Original: FontSystem_t makes Verdana bold 20/13/24 and italic 16 (CreateTTFont) and scales by the screen's height (GetScaleFromLowestResolution)
- Client: egui's Verdana at the size whose ascent plus descent is the cell height, regular whatever the weight; no screen-height scaling; CHAT is the chat bitmap font

- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/gui/font.rs:7`
- Decision: [x] port  [ ] leave
- Done (2026-11-19): The screen-height scaling is ported, and it is narrower than the note feared: FontSystem_t's constructor (GUI.dll 0x1012eef1) scales only two entries of its table (0x10272df0, size at +0xc) before CreateTTFont makes them: entry 4 (CC17, 20) becomes _ftol(20 * GetDisplayHeight / 768.0) (0x1012f09c..0x1012f0c7, the double at 0x101c4ff8), and entry 10 (TT_MIN12, 14) becomes _ftol(14 * ((y - 1) * 0.4 + 1)) where y is GetScaleFromLowestResolution's height over 480 (0x1012ef0f..0x1012ef49, the double 0.4 at 0x101a9150; DisplaySystem's drop-in display.rs confirms 640 by 480). Every other font keeps the table's size, so no other view's measure changes. gui/font.rs now has FontId::cell_on(height), used by Measure::egui_font and Measure::height with the egui screen's height (in the points the views are laid out in; no screen yet or in tests, the table's size). The original sizes them once at start; the client follows the window's height as it is. The weights were done before. Test: gui::font::tests::two_fonts_follow_the_screens_height (and font_table_weights).
- Done in part (2026-11-19, overnight): The weights are ported: FontSystem_t's table (GUI.dll 0x10272df0, read by the constructor 0x1012eef1) has a bold byte at +0x10 and an italic byte at +0x11 (read from GUI.dll itself: entries 4 CC17, 6 BOLD and 9 HUGE bold, 11 ITALIC italic), which CreateTTFont (0x1012ed48) turns into CreateFontA weight 700 / the italic flag. gui/font.rs now has FontId::style() and asks font.rs's new verdana_styled() for the system's verdanab.ttf / verdanai.ttf / verdanaz.ttf (regular Verdana stands in while the face loads or when the system lacks it). Left: the screen-height scaling (GetScaleFromLowestResolution, (scale - 1) * a constant + 1, and font 4 by GetDisplayHeight / a constant) is still egui's points; it would change every view's measured size, which wants a look at the screen. Test: gui::font::tests::font_table_weights.

The wheel: `RollupController_c`'s constructor (FUN_100489f9) calls FUN_10048822, which with the distributed value `MouseWheel` at 1 connects the controller's `WheelMoved` (the slot 0x1004a1b9 jumps to vtable +0x90) to the global wheel signal GlobalSignals +0x21c (emitted by `WindowController_c::HandleMouseWheel` 0x10157cec when no window is under the pointer), and disconnects it otherwise (it is reconnected when the value changes); the controller's `WheelMoved` (FUN_100487aa) is `ScrollBy(0, wheel.y * 40)` (the double at 0x101b0be0). The client: with `MouseWheel` 1 the wheel over the world now scrolls the column 40 a notch (`rollup::wheel`, viewer.rs's wheel handler, where 0 zooms and 2 does nothing as before). The scroll kept: the controller's destructor FUN_10048e92 saves `scroll_offset` (`GetScrollOffset().y`) with the pages, and FUN_100489f9 reads it back into +0x214; the client keeps it as a `scroll_offset <n>.<d>` line of rollup.ini (always with a decimal, and `parse` skips it, so no page is made of it), read when the file is loaded and written when a held scroll or a wheel notch ends. Left: the views' own smallest and largest heights and grid steps (FUN_100483ca holds a page's height to the view's +0x16c..+0x170 and FUN_1004836b snaps it to the step +0x174; the client's windows have no such sizes, so there is nothing to clamp by), the original's `scroll_offset` in `DockAreas/RollupArea.xml` when there is no rollup.ini yet (`aoprefs::rollup_pages` reads only the pages), and a view wider than the column still widens its page (the client's views are not all laid out to 192). Test `rollup::tests::the_column_scrolls_within_its_pages` (wheel step, the scroll's line kept and skipped as a page).
- Done in part (2026-11-19): The rollup area is now laid out and operated as GUI.dll's `RollupController_c` (FUN_100489f9) and `RollupPage_c` (FUN_10049a3c): the column is 192 pixels (the controller's 191, FUN_100486cb / 0x101b0d88; the notes' "175" is not in the code), pages touch with no gap (FUN_100488e5) and the column scrolls, held between none and the pages' height past it (`View::ScrollBy` 0x1014d269). A page (FUN_10049797, FUN_1004844c) is GFX_GUI_TAB_BACKGROUND, the black header of `PageHeaderView_c` (FUN_1004a740: GFX_GUI_WINDOW_ICON_I menu button 2 in, the title in font 5 eight to its right, the roll button and the close X 2 in at the right; the undock button is gone), its view 3 rows under the header as tall as its own `page_height`, and a 5-high 0x404040 grip; rolled up it is the header and one row. The page's own mouse (FUN_10049e00 / FUN_100484da / FUN_100484be): left press on the grip sizes the page, left double click rolls it, left press held scrolls the column, right press carries the page (FUN_100493f2, its title as the picture, put down by the next click through docks.rs); put down on the column a page or a dock window's tab goes in before the page under the pointer, else last, refused for the column's only page (FUN_10049121); put down elsewhere a page becomes a dock area window there (docks.rs `drop_from_column`; a window that is no dock view here becomes a free window there). The menu button gives the view's own menu, else text.mdb 10000 `CloseView` (FUN_10048c5c, FUN_10048de9). The black behind the column follows `cc_rollup_controller_fade_level` (FUN_100487ff, the AOU option page's slider). Page heights and rolled state are kept in rollup.ini (`name 1|0 height`, older lines still read) and, without that file, taken from the character's own `DockAreas/RollupArea.xml` (FUN_10048e92's `page_height`/`is_page_expanded`, `aoprefs::rollup_pages`); a view coming in takes its free window's room (FUN_10049f4a). The title-bar dock button stays only for the dockable windows that are not dock-area views here (Faction, PetWindow, Stats), whose tabs cannot be carried. #### `WIN-036` Stats not in the server's list shown as a dash

- SIMPLIFIED, medium

#### `WIN-040` Bitmap fonts drawn as a mesh with a 4-pixel line gap, behind a setting

- SIMPLIFIED, low
- Original: DisplaySystem draws FontSystem_t's bitmap fonts
- Client: each line is a mesh of glyph quads; line height is glyph height plus 4; the `original_font` setting (a checkbox, "The original's chat font") turns the bitmap fonts off for egui's font; a glyph not in the font takes a space's width
- A player notices: line spacing and fallback fonts are the client's
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/font.rs:65`; `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:2056`; `crates/mao-client/src/settings.rs:565`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Done in part (2026-11-19, overnight): The bitmap font's metrics were read: FontSystem_t::FontSystem_t (GUI.dll 0x1012eef1) reads a .fnt as two words, 255 glyph rectangles (0xff0 bytes), then a width table of 0x3fc bytes into +0x101c, adding one to each entry; the font's height +0xff0 is character 0x61's rectangle's height (9 for FontChat9/FontTooltip9, 12 for FontGameShell12), and TextRenderer_c::_UpdateWordSizes (0x1015dab9) uses +0xff0 as each word's height with no gap; FontInfo_t::GetGlyphWidth (0x1012eada) returns the table entry for codes below 0x100 and -1 above. The client now does the same (font.rs `parse_widths`, `line_height`, `advance`): lines are as high as 'a' (9, not 13), advances come from the width table (they differ from the rectangles' widths for FontChat9's codes 216 and up) and glyphs are drawn from the line's top (the client's own 2-pixel drop is gone). Code 0xff, which the original reads past its table, keeps a space's width; codes above 0xff advance -1. Left: the `original_font` setting (the client's switch, kept: players without the game's fonts or who prefer egui's) and DisplaySystem's own drawing of the fonts (not read). Test: `advances_are_the_width_table_and_lines_as_high_as_a`.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The bitmap font's line metrics in the original are not understood (WIN-085: FontSystem_t's bitmap FontInfo_t heights and DisplaySystem's text drawing were not read to the line gap), so the 4-pixel gap cannot be replaced with the original's number; the `original_font` setting is the client's switch for players without the bitmap fonts. Left until the bitmap font's metrics are read (FontInfo_t +0xff0 height, the .fnt header).

#### `WIN-078` Wheel: egui's own step, vertical bars only

- SIMPLIFIED, low
- Original: ScrollBar_c WheelMoved (0x10142820): 10 a notch
- Client: converts egui's 50-point notch to the original's step; the wheel only moves the vertical bar

- Where: `docs/CLIENT_UI.md:2030`; `crates/mao-client/src/gui/scroll.rs:277`

- Done (2026-11-19): Already as the original; nothing to port. `ScrollView_c::WheelMoved` (GUI.dll 0x10142820) only ever scrolls vertically: without snapping it scrolls by `Point(0, wheel.y * step)` (vtable +0xe4), with snapping it adds the wheel to its kept notches and uses their y alone (+0x1a8) against the vertical scroll offset; a horizontal bar is never moved by the wheel. When the view has no vertical bar (+0x170), no step (+0x154 <= 0) or its content fits its frame, the wheel goes on to the parent view (`GetParent()->WheelMoved`, +0x90). The routing: `GUIModule_c::MouseWheelMessage` (0x1012f93d) -> `WindowController_c::HandleMouseWheel` (0x10157cec) -> `Window::_HandleMouseWheel` (0x10154ab9), which gives it to the window's default wheel view (+0xa4, set only by `SetDefaultWheelView` 0x10154526, which nothing in GUI.dll or Gamecode.dll calls) or else its view at +0x84; with no window, the global wheel signal (the camera). The client's `gui/scroll.rs` `wheel` does the same (vertical only, false when there is no bar/step/room, and `gui/host.rs` then tries the next view out from under the pointer). The tests `gui::scroll` (wheel tests at scroll.rs:472-498) already cover the step and the snapping.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): ScrollBar_c::WheelMoved (0x10142820) moves its bar 10 a notch, and the client already converts egui's notch to that step; whether the original's wheel ever reaches a horizontal bar depends on which view WindowController_c sends the wheel to (the focused or hovered view's vertical bar), which was not read. Left.

#### `WIN-092` List double-click is a fixed 400 ms and sorting is by plain text keys

- GUESS, low
- Original: MultiListView_c's click count and sort comparison are the original's
- Client: a second click on the same row within 400 ms is a double click; rows sort by comparing key strings
- A player notices: double-click timing and sort order may differ
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/gui/multilist.rs:455`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19): Read further; nothing portable without a binary that is not decompiled. Sorting: `MultiListView_c::Sort` (GUI.dll 0x10136c92) sorts through `SlotCompareItems` (0x101334c8), which calls the row's own virtual compare (`MultiListViewItem_c` vtable slot 1, pure in the base class); each window's row class has its own rule, and the client's string keys already encode the rules read so far per window (e.g. `shop::row` from `InventoryListViewItem_c` FUN_1003dee6: the order it came in, the name without case, zero-padded numbers), so "plain text keys" is the mechanism, not a departure; a window whose compare was not read is that window's entry. Double click: the list does not time clicks; `MultiListView_c::MouseDown(point, button, clicks)` (0x10133c3f) passes the click count it is given to its down signal (FUN_10137b74), and the count comes from the input hot spot (`NewGuiSpot_t::CheckHotSpot` 0x1001db81: hot spot 1 is a press, 3 "LeftDoubleClick" sends `MouseDownMessage(1, 2)`), which `InputConfig_t::FrameProcess` (0x1001b253) takes from its list of `InputInfo_t` events already classified. What classifies a double click, and its time, is outside the decompiled DLLs: no AO binary handles WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK (0x203) or imports GetDoubleClickTime, and GUI.dll's timeGetTime users are not it; the events are made in the input layer (Interfaces.dll / the executable), which has no decompile here. Noticed: the original signals the double click on the second press (the down signal carries the count), the client on the second release.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): MultiListView_c's double click and sort comparison were not read tonight (its mouse handlers and the sort callback with the column's key kind); the client's 400 ms and string keys stay until they are.

#### `WIN-141` Score bars have no maximum; attack rating is the client's own sum

- MISSING, low
- Original: the score bars ask Gamecode for the next rank's score as their maximum; the attack rating is asked of Gamecode (stat 22)
- Client: duel, solo and team score bars have no maximum; the attack rating is the client's own sum
- A player notices: those bars show only a number with an empty fill; attack rating may differ
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/stats.rs:17`; `crates/mao-client/src/stats.rs:52`; `docs/GUI_DLL_PARITY.md:79`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Done in part (2026-11-19, overnight): The score bars are ported: StatView_c's FUN_1008049c fills the duel (684), solo (682) and team (683) score bars with FUN_1007fed3(N3Msg_GetPVPScoreForRank(N3Msg_GetPVPRank(stat) + 1), stat). Gamecode's score for a rank (FUN_1003ea89) is base^(rank - 1) * 20.0 cut to an int, times 100, with base = (float)pow(2500.0, 0.1111111119...) computed once (constants at 0x1015e760, 0x1015e758, 0x1015e750) and the power by FUN_1003dfc0's float squaring loop; the rank (FUN_1003eae2) is the first r in 1..10 with stat < score(r), less one (10 when none). stats.rs has pvp_score_for_rank, pvp_rank and next_rank_score, emulating the float products (rank 1 = 2000, rank 10 = 4,999,900: the f32 products fall just short of 2500), and the bars now have that maximum. Left: the attack rating row (stat 22 asked of Gamecode's stat holder; the client's own sum stays until the stat holder is ported, see WIN-036). Test: stats::tests::the_pvp_ranks_are_gamecodes.

#### `RND-004` Spell flight 0.45 s and landing 1.4 s are the client's own timings

- OWN-RULE, medium

- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19): Read further than the overnight reader: the original has no flight time and no landing time at all. The tracer (stat 419) is started by the casting character's animation event 0x42 during cast state 5 (FUN_100452d3 -> FUN_1004f989: NewHitLocation 0x7d1 -> 0x3ee, CreateEffect2), and flies by its own control (one per tracer kind, CreateGfxControlTracer 0x100d176c). The hit effects (stats 0x19e and 0x169 HitEffectType) are started on the target by the casting state machine FUN_1007b1e3 state 1 once the cast animation has run out (FUN_1003c6e7) and the spell succeeded (+0x28 == 1), not when the tracer arrives; each hit then lasts as its own controls say. Porting it means driving the shot from the caster's animation events and the cast state (the client's shots come from a message with no animation clock), plus each tracer control's run; that is the casting-state port, well over the time box for this entry.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The flight time is not one number in the original: _EffectHandler_t::CreateGfxControlTracer (Gamecode 0x100d176c) builds a different control for each tracer kind (0x3f5 FUN_100fe22f, 0x3fb FUN_100fec4e, 0x3fd FUN_100ff48e, 0x3fe FUN_100ff933, 0x400 FUN_10100268, 0x401 FUN_10100b0d, 0x402 FUN_101018ef, 0x403 FUN_101021eb, 0xbd2 FUN_10114e83), each with its own travel words, and the hit effect is started by the spell's own message timing; replacing the client's FLIGHT/LANDING means porting each tracer control's run and the hit's start, a set of effect ports (several catalogued on their own: RND-092, RND-110) well over the time box. Left.

#### `RND-056` Liquid tests ignore the zones' lists

- SIMPLIFIED, low
- Original: a zone's list of water infos is tested in order and stops at its first hit
- Client: every info of the playfield is tested in the order made

- Done in part (2026-11-19): Read the zone lists through: N3 `n3Playfield_t::GetLiquidSurfaceHeight` (0x1000cb1e; scratchpad n3.c) tests only the point's zone (`GetZoneInstance` 0x1000c97b) with `n3Zone_t::GetLiquidSurfaceHeight` (0x1001ab68: its list in order, the first info testing above 0 decides). Gamecode FUN_100b84b9 fills the lists: every info, in creation order (`GetFirstWaterInfo`/`GetNextWaterInfo` walk the push_back list), is `SetWater`-ed into the zone under each point of a zone-wide grid from its box minus one zone to its box plus one zone (the in-loop clamps are dead code). So the point's zone holds every info that contains the point, in the same relative order, and the client's test of all infos finds the same first hit; the playfield's (+0x90) and zone's (+0x1c) highest-top checks only skip what each info's own top test skips. No behaviour change outdoors (the catalog's "a different surface may be found" does not happen there); liquid.rs's comment now says so (commit 2afccc8). Left, two edge cases: a point off the tiles is looked up in zone 0 only (needs the playfield's zone size, n3Playfield_t +0x50, which the client does not read), and in a dungeon the grid points find their rooms at height 0 (PosToRoom), which needs the dungeon's rooms in liquid.rs.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The original tests a zone's own list of water infos (n3Zone_t's liquid data, per zone) in order; the client builds one list for the playfield from the definition's water triangles and has no per-zone split of them (the zones' liquid lists are made when N3 loads each zone). Splitting needs the zone each triangle belongs to, which was not read. Left.

#### `RND-068` Room left stays drawn two seconds

- SIMPLIFIED, low
- Original: hides the room when its locality monitor loses it
- Client: keeps the room just left for two seconds
- A player notices: the old room lingers briefly
- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/interior.rs:12`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19): Read further in N3 (scratchpad n3.c): `n3RoomMonitor_t` is an `n3CellMonitor_t` whose neighbour level is 2 (GetNeighborLevel 0x10003245). It shows a room on `OnCellChanged` (EnableRoom 0x10013611) and `DoorOpened` (0x10013561), hides it on `OnCellLost` (DisableRoom 0x10013702 via 0x100137a5) and two seconds after `DoorClosed` (Run 0x100135ab, _DAT_1003c968). `OnCellFound` only builds the VisualRoom hidden. So a room the character left stays drawn until the door to it closes (+2 s) or the locality loses it; when cells are found and lost by the neighbour level is decided by the locality source (`LocalitySource_t`, exported by Vehicle.dll / PathFinder.dll, not decompiled here), and which room DoorClosed is handed depends on the Gamecode callers. Without that rule, dropping the client's two-second linger would make rooms blink; left.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The original hides a room when its locality monitor loses it; the monitor's rules (which rooms it keeps, from where) were not read tonight, and the client's two seconds stand in for them to hide the gap while the next room's locality comes in. Removing the linger without the monitor's rule would make rooms blink. Left.

#### `RND-097` Weather fade rolls the old state at full strength

- SIMPLIFIED, low
- Original: Environment_t keeps a current and next table and lerps by the fade (FUN_100bd555 / FUN_100bf96e)
- Client: the new state is blended with the previous state at full strength, weighted by one minus the fade
- A player notices: the fade between weather states may differ in detail
- Where: `crates/mao-formats/src/weather.rs:287`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19): Read through: Environment_t's frame (FUN_100bd555, run for every environment of the playfield each frame by FUN_100beacd) keeps two tables, 0 (+0xc, the output) and 1 (+0x10), and two count-downs +0x14 / +0x18 that drop by ONE PER FRAME (0x100bd60e..0x100bd64e: the step is 1, 0 only when the frame's delta GameTime+0x78 equals the never-set int +0x50, i.e. a paused frame). When +0x18 runs out, table 1 is rolled for the state now in force (FUN_100b14f9 then FUN_100bcec6(1): its values scaled by the fade weight w = elapsed / fade) and +0x18 is set to fade / 255 (the double at 0x10167fa0) while it still fades, else to length - elapsed; +0x14 is set to length - elapsed each time. When +0x14 runs out, table 0 is rolled for the PREVIOUS state (FUN_100b149b, state +0x28; elapsed past its length, so at full strength). Each time either fires, table 0 = lerp(table 0, table 1, w) (FUN_100bf96e) — cumulatively. So in the original the old state is lerped away within a few seconds (a step every one or two frames, each by w), not over the whole fade, and how fast depends on the frame rate (the count-downs count frames, though they are set from seconds). The client computes the weather on the network thread as a pure function of the clock (areas.rs blend_with_weather, called twice a loop from net.rs) for the playfield's own and every area's environment; the faithful port needs a per-environment state machine stepped once per rendered frame, which the client's network-thread computation has no place for, and its result would still hang on the frame rate. Left with these findings (the client's linear fade-out of the old state is the outcome the original's numbers suggest was meant: 255 steps over the fade).
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The original's Environment_t keeps a current and a next 22-float table (FUN_100bd555) and lerps them by the fade (FUN_100bf96e: the first 18 floats by the weight, 0x12-0x14 by the weights' share of +0x15). Those tables are built by FUN_100bcec6 from the area's environment, a different shape from the client's 14 rolled weather values (weather.rs roll); porting the fade means porting the table building too. Over the time box. Left.

#### `RND-137` Statels of generated buildings and rendering effects get no effects

- MISSING, high

- Done (2026-11-19): The last part of the entry is finished, with two findings that change what it said. (1) The rendering effects: DisplaySystem FUN_1006d49a (the VisualMesh_t set-up) gives effect 1, 2 or 3 to a mesh with a connector named eff_hologram/eff_space/eff_clear, the last such connector counting; FUN_1006c61d applies the effect's delta state and FUN_1006c005 draws it. A scan of every mesh type in the resource database (mao-db grep), and of cd_image and Setupf, finds one such mesh: the asteroid 0x403b7 (EP03_RUBIKA_asteroidbig2, one statel of playfield 109), which has eff_space. No mesh names eff_hologram or eff_clear, and the hologram's textures 0x28022/0x28023 are in no texture type of the database. So space is ported and the other two are not: there is nothing in the game to draw with them. Space now works like this: mao_formats::attractors::rendering_effect picks the effect from the connector names; model::build_animated gives every part of the mesh Material::effect. Under space the materials' own states are not applied (FUN_1006c005 draws the simple meshes with SpaceDeltaState alone), so the parts are drawn opaque, whole, one-sided and writing depth, and the renderer leaves out the fog (no_fog, the shader's flags.z). (2) The templates 12200, 12570 and 96003 were in gfxtweak.bin all along. "Not in the file" was wrong: the client had no look for their classes, and CreateGfxControl (Gamecode 0x100cfdc6) makes both. Kind 3014 is _GfxControlVein_t: Gamecode FUN_10103396, FUN_10103026 the words, FUN_10102e1a the visual plus the fire 12205 at its foot, FUN_10102c87 the run. DisplaySystem's GfxVisualVein draws it: FUN_1002def9 the strands on the B-spline FUN_10004484/FUN_100043c3, FUN_1002d79f the turned second pass, FUN_1002e6d1 the draw. It is now ported as gfx::Vein and effects::vein_shells. 12200 is the Shadowlands' veins (some 20 playfields) and 96003 the beam of the Whom-Pah pillars (30 Rubi-Ka playfields). Kind 3019 is _GfxControlTrail_t: FUN_10102857, FUN_101024de the words, FUN_10102566 Init(50, colour, width, life, texture), FUN_10102331 the run. DisplaySystem's GfxVisualTrail draws it (FUN_1002b486: samples every twentieth of a second in rings of 1000, ribbons walked back 2.5 a step; mode 0 one ribbon facing the view, mode 1 four from the samples' orientations). It is now ported as gfx::Trail, effects::TrailRing and effects::trail_shells. 12570 is the ships' engine trail; 71000 and 71003 are the drop ships' and bombers'. Statel effects and placed effects (the script meshes' universal effects) now lay their shells as well as their sparks. A placed effect now carries its object's turn (FXS Rotation) for the trails' orientations. The offline `map` picture with MAO_STATEL_EFFECTS shows the veins too (looked at for playfields 505 and 4885). Not covered here: a ship that is a dynel rather than a script object has no connector effects in this client at all, and a universal effect still starts at its object's place rather than its connector's (both known before this work). Tests: attractors::tests::connector_names_give_the_rendering_effects, mao-render tests::the_space_effect_draws_without_fog, game_data the_asteroid_is_drawn_under_the_space_effect / the_connectors_veins_are_veins_with_their_fire / the_ships_trails_are_trails, effects::tests::a_vein_s_strands_climb_and_fade_as_its_visual_draws_them / a_trail_lays_ribbons_back_along_its_samples; mao-client bin tests 688 passed.
- Done in part (2026-11-18): Done: statel effects in a generated building (a mission's) and in an interior of rooms take the props' placing by their rooms; the Arete capture's alien ship has its 21 effects inside its rooms (none before, and a shop's stood at places inside their rooms' own frames). Left: eff_hologram, eff_space and eff_clear are ways a mesh is drawn (DisplaySystem's rendering effects 1 to 3), which this client has no draw for; the templates 12200, 12570 and 96003 are not in the effects' file and where the original has them was not found.

#### `RND-140` Statel zones of the second layout are not read

- MISSING, medium
- Original: n3Zone_t loader reads a zone's lights and packed block; room objects at the end of each zone
- Client: a zone that begins with a packed block and lights has its lights read past and no statels kept; a zone fitting neither layout is left out

- Where: `crates/mao-formats/src/statels.rs:19`; `docs/ROADMAP.md:73`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Done in part (2026-11-19): The zone reader is ported whole. The original never tells the two layouts apart by their bytes: a room playfield's zones (its rooms: n3RoomMonitor_t::EnableRoom 0x10013611 -> n3StatelController_t::EnableRoomStatels 0x10025ae8 -> the loader built by FUN_100274b1, flag +8 clear) are read by FUN_10027f16 (a size word, a count and the zlib-packed 565 colours, FUN_1002a180 = zlib 1.2.5 uncompress; then two lists of 18-byte lights, FUN_10027d90, the first list's alpha capped at 100), an outdoor one's (MapZonesInViewcone -> FUN_10028fe7 -> FUN_1002739d, flag set) by FUN_10027cb2 (a list of u16 indices of the global statels the zone holds, two statel lists); then the run (FUN_10028029, the vtable 0x1003e64c slot 4) reads two statel lists and the light objects (FUN_10026e66: position, packed turn, kind byte, RGB, and for kinds 2/4 the SetLight numbers; bit 7 = not made) for both. The colours are handed to the statels by FUN_100271b6 (a word of count each, two words from data version 10, RDBPlayfield_t +0x64) and reach VisualMesh_t::SetVertexColours (FUN_100240a5). statels.rs now has Layout, Zone, Light, LightMesh, read_zone/parse_zones/parse_as and Statel::light; the client picks the layout from the playfield definition (main.rs statel_layout: rooms::parse has rooms), also for the booth/door/sign lookups; tools keep a file-level guess (guess_layout). This also settles RND-123 (the client's old "whichever reads to the end" rule): it had taken room zones of playfields 1186, 1187, 4221 and 9070 for tiles (four stray statels, and 90 wrong statels for 815 in one zone of 4221). Tests: statels::zone_tests::{a_room_zone, a_tile_zone}; game_data every_playfields_statel_zones (all 624 files: every zone reads to its end in its definition's layout, the guess agrees, only those four playfields change; 209,765 of 213,272 room statels coloured, 193,436 with exactly one colour per vertex of their mesh in the original's hand-out order, model::colour_order). LEFT, with the reason: drawing what is now read. (1) The statels' colours are per statel (each its own copy, applied as the original's trimesh draws), while the client draws a mesh's parts once for all statels as instances: giving them means per-statel geometry (3.9 million coloured vertices in playfield 362 alone, thousands of extra draw calls) or a per-instance colour buffer in mao-render's instance records (Model::instances and the shader's part record, used across the client); either needs the result looked at and its memory and frame time measured in the running client. The data and the vertex order (model::colour_order) are ready for it; as emissive vertex colours like the rooms' light maps (randy31 lightmap_data: emissive source = vertex colour when the material's emissive is dark). (2) The zone lights and light objects are point/spot lights (VisualMesh_t::SetLight); the client's renderer lights by sun and ambient only, so they need a local-light system in mao-render first.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The zone is read off the main thread in the original: n3StatelController_t::EnableRoomStatels (N3.dll 0x10025ae8) builds a zone object (FUN_1002896c) and schedules a WorkerRequest_c (FUN_100274b1) that reads the zone from the .pf file; the statel reader inside it is FUN_1002777a (read for RND-141). The reader of the zone's own header (the packed block and the 18-byte lights) is in that worker's run function, reached only through its vtable, which the scratchpad N3 decompile (n3.c) does not have in a readable form tonight. Porting it means a second zone reader in statels.rs checked against every playfield's file, and how the two layouts are told apart (RND-123); over 40 minutes with no reader to copy. Left.

#### `RND-170` Sequencer effects: end cutting child's duration, loop 0x400, flag 0x800

- MISSING, low

Surveyed gfxtweak.bin: 56 of the 522 entries carry an end, their children of kinds 2007 (30, bundles: what a bundle does with its own +0x10 not read), 3003 (12), 2004 (5, mode 4), 3031 and 3023 (3 each), 3006, 1018, 3020; 49 of the 118 sequencers loop (0x400), 7 have 0x800. A faithful port needs the cut as each child visual's word-8 duration (a set_duration over ~20 Visual kinds) and, for most of the cut entries, looping effects (an effect that never ends, through pulse_timing and every visual function's Delayed arm in effects.rs) plus the bundles' duration rule; over the time box for a low entry. Left with these findings.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The sequencer's end cutting a child's duration needs a new limited-duration visual handled by every visual function (particles, meshes, trails, shells, timing) in effects.rs; 0x400 looping and 0x800 (running without the dynel) need the scheduler's state. #### `RND-177` Statels' moving parts all play on the clock

- MISSING, low
- Original: statels' parts follow their state (AnimPlay/AnimPos) the way things do
- Client: the playfield statels' moving parts are drawn at the clock's time; things the server announces do follow their AnimPlay/AnimPos

- Decision: [x] port  [ ] leave
- Done (2026-11-19): Already the original's behaviour; no change. DisplaySystem's LODManager::Process (drop-in lodmanager.rs `process`) gives every watched 0xf6951 statel mesh the time each frame (`add_animation_time`) while its global `animate` byte is set; that byte starts at 1 (globals at 0x100ae1a4) and nothing writes it: no setter in DisplaySystem, and Gamecode's only LODManager calls are AOPlayfieldCityHolderClient_c::Enable/DisableVisibility (0x1012eadb / 0x1012ea59: AddMesh / RemoveMesh). Playfield statels are not dynels and have no AnimPlay/AnimPos of their own; the things the server announces do follow theirs in the client already (net.rs prop_anim_time). So the playfield statels' moving parts run on the clock in the original too.
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): Partly a misreading: DisplaySystem's LODManager::Process gives every 0xf6951 statel mesh the time each frame when its animate flag is set (drop-in lodmanager.rs, global `animate` = 1), so statels' moving parts do run on the clock in the original. Whether a statel's part can also be stopped by a state (as things are by AnimPlay/AnimPos) depends on the statel's own messages, which were not seen. Left.

#### `RND-178` Sun rays do not flicker

- MISSING, low
- Original: VisualSunRays_t (FUN_1005a3a9) flickers the rays by a table

VisualSunRays_t's frame (DisplaySystem FUN_1005a3a9) gives ray i the alpha (255 − table[(i & 7) + (+0x32c & 1) × 8]) × alpha / 255 in whole numbers and the centre the plain alpha; +0x32c is only ever cleared (FUN_10059f44), so the first eight waves are used. The client's fxs/visuals.rs keeps the phase (advanced by the GAME object's GameDeltaTime each frame), builds the table (flicker_table) and sets each ray's alpha so. ### Network and protocol: an approximation or a stand-in (2)

#### `NET-001` Character creation logs in on a new connection per request

- SIMPLIFIED, low
- Original: not stated (the original's creation module stays on its login connection)
- Client: every suggest/create request logs in again on a new connection

- Where: `crates/mao-client/src/charcreate.rs:182`
- Decision: [ ] port  [ ] leave
- Looked at, left (2026-11-19, overnight): The original's creation runs on the login connection it already has (the character list's), but the client's launcher closes that connection as soon as the list is read, because the game runs in a process of its own that must make its own login (LCH-001; "the login connection must be gone before the game's own login", launcher.rs `log_in`). Keeping one connection open through the creation means holding it across the launcher's stages and closing it before Play: a restructuring of the launcher's threads for a wait of under a second per request; left.

### Network and protocol: a guard or fallback the original lacks (3)

#### `NET-008` Network time-outs and non-blocking polling

- SAFETY, low
- Original: not stated
- Client: 20 s time-out on sends and on waits for login or chat replies; the world connection reads non-blocking and polls because read time-outs on Windows left the socket undefined
- A player notices: a slow server is given up on after 20 s

Removing them would make the client hang where the original gives up.
